item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine has deployed naval drones to strike Russian warships in Libya’s Benghazi port, claiming lawful self-defence, while Russia has violated Finnish airspace with a helicopter and Polish airspace with an unmanned aerial vehicle. NATO’s chief has pledged defence against a Russian space threat after reports of a planned nuclear satellite launch, and MI5 has warned UK firms supplying Ukraine of sabotage risk. The UN Security Council warned that winter attacks on Ukraine’s power grid and Black Sea shipping threaten lives and global food supplies. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed a Hamas political official, his wife, a senior education official appointed by Hamas, and several others, while Hamas is weighing its response to the attacks. Settlers demolished a Palestinian home in a West Bank village and threatened an ancient mikveh, actions the IDF called a serious criminal act. The Gaza Board of Peace reported encouragement from recent conversations with Netanyahu, even as Israeli officials threaten a large-scale offensive and displacement of Palestinians. Kushner described the destruction in Gaza as a "good thing". The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel and Hezbollah: the situation
item.description:
Israeli air forces have intensified strikes in Lebanon, hitting Hezbollah rockets, launchers in the Beqaa Valley and targets in eastern Lebanon. Hezbollah’s leader again demanded the release of five detained operatives and rejected any post-UNIFIL force outside U.N. authority, while Iran’s support for Hezbollah was reaffirmed. The two sides are preparing for an eighth round of peace talks before year-end. The conflict has caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Iran launched a drone strike that hit Kuwait, killing two Italian nationals, and Iran denied responsibility for the attack. Iran is also reported to be racing to build an underground facility between key nuclear sites. The conflict continues with missile activity in the region, and the UCDP recorded 123 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
ISIL carried out a suicide attack in Hasakah that killed two Syrian security force members and injured several others, and a separate suicide bombing in Tartous wounded a security officer and killed the gunman. The Syrian government is considering a law to grant nationality to children of foreign fighters, reflecting concerns about the legacy of extremist participation. Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Jordan issued condemnations of attacks on Syrian security facilities, showing regional diplomatic responses. Syrian authorities seized Iranian weapons destined for Lebanon, indicating ongoing arms interdiction efforts. 2,732 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Baghdad has moved troops to secure Kurdish borders after the top court authorized a military presence and the takeover of border posts and oil fields, while the prime minister pushes for greater central authority over the Kurdish region. The defense ministry ordered nationwide troop deployment and the closure of oil smuggling routes, and a drone strike destroyed a militant vehicle in Anbar province. Hezbollah fighters were transferred onto Popular Mobilization Forces payroll, and Germany arrested an Iraqi duo suspected of plotting synagogue attacks. An Iraqi court sentenced eight French nationals to life imprisonment for IS group membership, and UCDP recorded 396 battle-related deaths in 2024.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
RSF forces have intensified drone strikes, hitting a United Nations building and residential areas in Khartoum and killing four people, while a separate drone attack in Blue Nile state killed 19 civilians and displaced thousands near Ed Damazin. RSF-aligned troops assaulted aid offices in Nyala and a shelter in West Kordofan, causing civilian casualties. A RSF counterintelligence chief and a commander defected to the Sudanese army in Khartoum, indicating shifting loyalties. Ethiopia offered to host inclusive Sudan peace talks and propose a national unity government, but Sudan rejected the offer, questioning Ethiopia's neutrality. The conflict produced 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Somali federal forces and U.S. airstrikes have recently killed dozens of al-Shabaab militants in Lower Shabelle, while Turkish-made missiles were identified in a deadly airstrike in Puntland, linking the conflict to external weapon supplies. The parliament speaker has accused Kenya, Ethiopia and Uganda of colluding with al-Shabaab, and the president has blamed the UAE for financing armed groups, while the Somali government warned that Houthi support could boost al-Shabaab's attack capabilities. Foreign troops are beginning to withdraw from Somalia, raising concerns that al-Shabaab could expand its influence. The United States has reversed its funding for international military support to Somalia. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Militant groups in Nigeria's Niger state carried out a reprisal attack that killed at least 30 civilians and later deployed more tactical teams, while separate assaults killed 11 soldiers in the southeast, 16 near the Malian border and 25 in another strike. Fulani communities suffered mass killings of at least 64 people, and a Saudi national was kidnapped by suspected Islamic State militants in Niger. Insurgents have begun using off-the-shelf drones, and rebels in Mali claim Ukrainian officers are training them on drone tactics. The Sahel jihadist insurgency caused 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen attacked a Plateau community, killing 16 and injuring four, while suspected militants killed at least 30 people in Niger state. Bandits abducted six people in Kaduna and six in Chikun LGA, and gunmen opened fire on Peter Obi supporters in Edo, injuring one person. President Tinubu pledged to rescue abducted schoolchildren in Borno and to intensify operations against terrorists, while law enforcement officials reaffirmed a refusal to negotiate with bandits. Amnesty International condemned the Tinubu government for inaction after a mass burial of Plateau victims. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Eastern DR Congo: the situation
item.description:
M23 rebels have pulled back from the area around Bunia but have opened a new front near the Uganda border and are advancing toward Uvira city. WHO evacuated its Ebola response team from an Ituri hospital after fighting trapped them, and the Ebola death rate is now near 50% as cases surpass 12,000. Rebels claim to have shot down a Congolese military aircraft, which has gone missing, and a South African mercenary was captured in the aftermath. The conflict has displaced 8.2 million people and caused 1,158 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Boko Haram insurgents have reappeared in northern Cameroon, adding a new security threat to the already volatile region. In a remote national park, elephants killed a Swiss tourist and wounded a British and an American hiker, forcing other hikers to hide in tree stumps. item.title: Central African Republic: the situation
item.description:
CAR forces have completed Rwanda special forces and basic special operations training and have neutralised 34 Boko Haram and ISWAP fighters in the Lake Chad area. The UN Security Council renewed the MINUSCA mandate to 2027, lowered the troop ceiling to 12,000 and ordered a gradual drawdown while extending the mission. Saudi backing now funds a second year of a Sahel counter-terrorism programme centred on Chad, and tensions have risen between Chad and Niger after a prison break in Chad that caused two inmate deaths and 30 escapes. Wagner’s gold interests continue to block peace efforts, and 246 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:

President Kiir told an Oil and Power conference that partnerships, not speeches, must change lives, after travelling to Ethiopia and holding investment talks with Saudi Arabia in Riyadh.
